prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, full body shot, head to toe. ONE woman standing, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, the camera set back so her whole body fits in the frame from the top of her head to her feet, her face still sharp. Mid 20s.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult French woman in French red-lip makeup — fair natural skin with a light dewy finish, softly brushed natural brows, a barely-there brown liner and fluttering lashes, no eyeshadow, soft natural colour on the cheeks, large eyes with bright real catchlights, a single bold classic red lip with a soft matte finish, long dark-brown hair in an effortless tousled updo, an unbothered, effortless expression. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. A single thick gold hoop hangs on each ear.

Physique: A towering giantess on an even scale at full head-to-toe height — massive rounded shoulders, huge thick arms, a colossal full chest, a broad heavy torso with a large smooth rounded belly, wide solid hips, enormous columnar thighs running long into thick calves and long legs to the floor. No single part stands out more than another.

Body: from the collarbones down her whole body — both shoulders, both arms and hands, her chest, belly, hips, both legs and both feet — is not painted, covered or clothed but physically carved from ONE solid block of dark wenge wood, a deep near-black wood finely striped with narrow gold-tan pinstripes running through it, polished to a hard satin sheen, completely opaque, one continuous sculpted mass, never hollow, with no seam and no skin anywhere, every wrist, palm, finger, knuckle and toe the same carved wood, the pinstripe grain flowing unbroken down through every joint all the way to her toes. Her extreme platform stiletto sandals are carved from the same block of wenge as her legs, the grain running unbroken through the ankle, the instep and every toe, nothing painted on the foot.

Opacity: everything below the collarbones is solid, completely opaque carved wenge — no light passes through it at any point. It has the same dense, fibrous solidity throughout, catching light only as soft satin sheen along the grain, never glowing from within. Her face, by contrast, is warm, soft, living flesh, its natural colour nowhere close to the colour of the wood.

Boundary: a sharp jagged line runs around the base of the neck and across both collarbones — real skin above, material immediately below, and nowhere else on her body does real skin appear again. At that line, the wood's edge rises in a small raised step above her flesh, casting a crisp shadow — her skin beside it stays smooth and even. Shards interlock along this line only, every edge solid all the way through.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a deep charcoal grey on one side and a warm gold on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a matte dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, body angled 45 degrees, feet planted apart, her left hand (solid material) resting on her flared hip, her right arm held clear of her body with the hand (solid material) relaxed at hip height, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: two large softboxes rake across her body from either side, so charcoal-grey light glances off the left half and gold light glances off the right half, catching in the grain as soft highlights all the way down to her carved sandals. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only. Only her face, ears and neck read as real skin. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
